researchMethod: Phase 6 scale-out - filings fetched/extracted programmatically (research.js), analysis performed directly by Claude Code reading the extracted material, not by an automated LLM API call. Every factual claim below cites a specific source in the sources[] list.

quantContext.note: From this project's own scoring pipeline (companies.json + screener.js, Phases 1-5/7), included for reference only - not itself a research source.

whyCheapBearCase.answer: NKE stock has fallen 30.9% over six months [source: 1], and the FY2026 10-K (fiscal year ended May 31, 2026) directly documents a multi-year earnings collapse that explains the discount: net income fell from $5,700 million in FY2024 to $3,219 million in FY2025 to $3,108 million in FY2026 - a 45.5% two-year decline - while diluted EPS fell from $3.73 (FY2024) to $2.16 (FY2025) to $2.10 (FY2026) [source: 2]. Management's own 'Factors Impacting Our Business' section names specific, ongoing structural problems: 'a trend of declining store traffic, elevated promotional activity and higher levels of inventory across the marketplace' in Greater China, and Converse brand revenue down 31% year-over-year as it undergoes 'a strategic reset,' with management explicitly stating 'we expect negative impacts from Greater China and Converse to continue throughout fiscal 2027' [source: 2, 3]. The company also recognized $385 million of employee severance charges in FY2026 and says it 'may take additional actions which could lead to additional charges in future quarters' [source: 2]. The 10-K also discloses NIKE is 'currently subject to multiple securities class action and shareholder derivative lawsuits relating to a drop in our stock price' [source: 4] - a real, filed, ongoing litigation risk tied directly to the stock decline itself.

revenueEpsTrend.answer: Roughly flat revenue with declining GAAP earnings and margin, in the context of a much larger two-year decline. FY2026 (ended May 31, 2026) revenue was $46,398 million versus $46,309 million in FY2025, up 0.2% reported but down 2% on a currency-neutral basis, versus $51,362 million in FY2024 (FY2025 was down 10% from FY2024) [source: 2, 6]. Net income fell to $3,108 million in FY2026 from $3,219 million in FY2025 (-3.4%) and from $5,700 million in FY2024 [source: 2, 6]. Diluted EPS was $2.10 in FY2026 versus $2.16 in FY2025 (-2.8%) and $3.73 in FY2024 [source: 2, 6]. By segment, NIKE Brand wholesale revenue grew 6% reported ($27.5B vs $25.9B) while NIKE Direct fell 6% reported ($17.7B vs $18.8B), with NIKE Brand Digital down 12% - a real channel-mix shift, not just aggregate softness [source: 2]. So the picture is: FY2025 was a severe down year versus FY2024, and FY2026 has essentially stabilized at that lower level (flat-to-slightly-down revenue, modestly declining net income) rather than continuing to deteriorate or clearly recovering.

marginTrend.answer: Gross margin improved modestly while net margin declined, due to a higher tax rate rather than operating deterioration. FY2026 gross margin was 42.9% versus 42.7% in FY2025 (+20bps), which the 10-K attributes to lower warehousing/logistics costs, favorable currency, and lower other costs, partially offset by lower Converse gross margin and higher NIKE Brand product costs [source: 2]. EBIT margin also improved slightly to 8.3% from 8.2% [source: 2]. However, net income margin fell to 6.7% from 7.0%, because the effective tax rate rose sharply to 20.3% from 17.1% (+320bps), which management attributes primarily to a prior-year one-time non-cash deferred tax benefit that did not recur [source: 2]. All of these FY2026 figures remain far below FY2024's levels (net income margin 11.1%, EBIT margin 12.7%) [source: 2], so while the year-over-year trend from FY2025 to FY2026 is roughly stable-to-slightly-improving at the operating level, the multi-year level of profitability remains deeply depressed versus FY2024.

guidanceChange.answer: Not determinable with a specific numeric figure from the extracted filing text - no explicit forward-looking revenue or EPS guidance range was captured in the MD&A or Risk Factors excerpts pulled for this pass. The 10-K does disclose qualitative forward-looking commentary: management expects 'negative impacts from Greater China and Converse to continue throughout fiscal 2027' and expects the multi-year 'Product Management, Marketplace Management, and Brand Management' restructuring actions to be substantially complete 'by the end of December 2026' [source: 3]. A 10-K risk factor also separately warns that 'the scope and time horizon of any guidance we provide may change from period to period' [source: 4], which is boilerplate language about guidance volatility risk rather than a specific guidance change itself.

catalysts.text: IEEPA tariff recovery: following a February 20, 2026 U.S. Supreme Court ruling that certain IEEPA-based tariffs were unauthorized, NIKE recognized a $986 million benefit in Cost of sales for recovery of tariffs previously paid, 'largely offsetting the impact of the IEEPA tariffs recognized during fiscal 2026' - a concrete, dated, quantified one-time financial benefit, of which $302 million had been received and $684 million remained receivable as of May 31, 2026 (with the filing noting substantially all of the remainder was received shortly after fiscal year-end).

North America has 'made the most progress' against the company's product/marketplace/brand turnaround actions, per management's own segment-by-segment progress assessment, while apparel revenue grew 4% reported (2% currency-neutral) - signs the turnaround is gaining traction in at least some parts of the business even as Greater China and Converse remain weak.

NIKE Brand wholesale revenue grew 6% reported (4% currency-neutral) in FY2026, driven by higher North America revenue - a reversal of the prior NIKE Direct-first strategy that management is now actively 'repositioning NIKE Brand Digital as a full-price platform and reinvesting in wholesale distribution.'

risks.text: Ongoing, explicitly disclosed securities class action and shareholder derivative litigation relating to the stock price decline - a real, filed, currently active legal risk, not a hypothetical one.

Management's own forward-looking statement that Greater China and Converse will continue to have negative impacts 'throughout fiscal 2027' - i.e., two of the company's identified problem areas are explicitly not expected to be resolved in the near term.

Continued restructuring costs: $385 million of severance charges were recognized in FY2026 alone, and management states it 'may take additional actions which could lead to additional charges in future quarters' - an open-ended, not-yet-fully-quantified cost risk.

verdict.reasoning: The filing evidence shows NIKE's earnings collapse (FY2024 to FY2025) has stopped getting worse and arguably stabilized in FY2026 - revenue and EBIT margin were both roughly flat-to-slightly-up year-over-year, and a large one-time IEEPA tariff recovery ($986 million) provided real, quantified relief [source: 2]. That is consistent with 'opportunity' if the turnaround continues. But the structural risks are also filing-confirmed and specific, not speculative: management itself says Greater China and Converse weakness will persist through fiscal 2027, ongoing securities class-action litigation exists specifically because of the stock decline, and further restructuring charges are explicitly flagged as possible [source: 2, 3, 4]. Given that FY2026 net income and diluted EPS still declined year-over-year even after the tariff-recovery tailwind, and profitability remains roughly 40% below FY2024 levels [source: 2, 6], I would not call this a clean 'opportunity' yet - it is a business still mid-turnaround with real, management-acknowledged unresolved problem areas. Confidence is medium because the trajectory (stabilizing vs. still deteriorating) is genuinely ambiguous from two fiscal years of data alone, and I could not confirm current specific forward guidance.

sourcingNote: The Q3 FY2026 10-Q's own MD&A/Risk Factors extraction blocks in the packet were mostly boilerplate (critical accounting estimates disclaimer and Item 2/5 share repurchase and Rule 10b5-1 administrative content) rather than substantive results discussion, so the 10-Q was used only for the risk-factor 'no material changes' confirmation and buyback-pause detail (share repurchases were paused since Q1 FY2026, none in the quarter ended February 28, 2026) - the bulk of the quantitative analysis above instead relies on the FY2026 10-K, which contains full three-year Results of Operations detail. Of the 6 cached news headlines, two were clearly NKE-specific ('What Does Nike (NKE) Gain From Its Victor Wembanyama Signature Shoe Bet?' and 'Are International Logistics Improvements Paying Off for NIKE?') but were not cited above because only their headlines were cached (no article body), and neither headline by itself supports a specific factual claim beyond what the filings already establish; the remaining headlines (Dick's Sporting Goods, generic 'dow jones stocks moving' pieces, a back-to-school consumer piece) were not NKE-specific enough to cite.
